title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 75 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 456–459 (Night 75, continuing directly from nights-74), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 75 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Nuzhat al-Zamān, hearing the stranger’s verses from behind her litter curtain, recognises her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān; the two faint, revive, and tell each other their stories. The chamberlain who married her learns who she is, and the stoker, fearing the worst, is run down by the servant’s men. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَالسَّبْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu wa-al-sabʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fifth and the seventy,
sentences.i: And when it was the seventy-fifth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ لَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ قَالَتِ اللَّهُ يَجْمَعُ شَمْلَهُ بِمَنْ يُحِبُّ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna nuzhata al-zamāni lammā samiʿat kalāmahu qālati allāhu yajmaʿu shamlahu bi-man yuḥibbu
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Nuzhat al-Zamān, when she heard his speech, said: God gathers his union with the one-who he loves.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Nuzhat al-Zamān heard his words she said, “May God bring him together again with the one he loves.”
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words. The imperfect يجمع is read as a wish.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِلْخَادِمِ قُلْ لَهُ اِسْمَعْنِي شَيْأً مِنْ مُفَارَقَتِكَ لِأَهْلِكَ وَوَطَنِكَ فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ كَمَا أَمَرَتْهُ سَيِّدَتُهُ فَصَعَّدَ الزَّفَرَاتِ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat li-al-khādimi qul lahu isʿmaʿnī shayʾan min mufāraqatika li-ahlika wa-waṭanika fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu kamā amaratʰu sayyidatuhu fa-ṣaʿʿada al-zafarāti wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then she said to the servant: Say to him: Make-me-hear something of your parting from your family and your homeland. And the servant said to him as his mistress had commanded him, and he sent-up the sighs and recited these verses.
sentences.i: Then she said to the servant, “Tell him: let me hear something of how you came to leave your family and your homeland.” The servant told him just as his mistress had bidden him, and he heaved up sighs and recited these verses:

sentences.t:
اَمَا وَهَوَاهَا حِلْفَةً عِنْدَ ذِي وَجْدِ * لَاُكْرِمُ دَاراً قَدْ اَحَلَّتْ بِهَا هِنْدُ
هَوَاهَا هَوًى لَايَعْرِفُ النَّاسُ غَيْرَهُ * فَلَيْسَ لَهُ قَبْلُ وَلَيْسَ لَهُ بَعْدُ
كَأَنَّ ثَرَى الْوَادِي مُمَسَّكُ عَنْبَرِ * اِذَا مَا جَرَتْ يَوْماً بِسَاحَتِهِ هِنْدُ
سَلَامٌ عَلَى مَحْبُوبَةٍ بِرِبَا الْحِمَى * عَزِيزَةِ قَوْمٍ كُلُّ مَنْ حَوْلَهَا عَبْدُ
خَلِيلَيَّ مَا بَعْدَ الْعَشِيَّةِ مَنْزِلُ * اَرِيحَا فَهَذَا الْبَانُ وَالْعَلَمُ الْفَرْدُ
فَلَا نَسَاً لَا مِنْ غَيْرِ قَلْبِي فَاِنَّهُ * حَلِيفُ هَوًى لَا يُسْتَطَاعُ لَهُ رَدُّ
سَقَى اللَّهُ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ سَحَائِباً * مِسَحَّاً فَلَا يَنْفَكُّ عَنْ مَتْنِهَا رَعْدُ
sentences.tr:
amā wa-hawāhā ḥilfatan ʿinda dhī wajdi * la-ukrimu dāran qad aḥallat bihā hindu
hawāhā hawan lā yaʿrifu al-nāsu ghayrahu * fa-laysa lahu qablu wa-laysa lahu baʿdu
ka-anna tharā al-wādī mumassaku ʿanbarin * idhā mā jarat yawman bi-sāḥatihi hindu
salāmun ʿalā maḥbūbatin bi-ribā al-ḥimā * ʿazīzati qawmin kullu man ḥawlahā ʿabdu
khalīlayya mā baʿda al-ʿashiyyati manzilu * arīḥā fa-hādhā al-bānu wa-al-ʿalamu al-fardu
fa-lā nasāʾ lā min ghayri qalbī fa-innahu * ḥalīfu hawan lā yustaṭāʿu lahu raddu
saqā allāhu nuzhata al-zamāni saḥāʾiban * misaḥḥan fa-lā yanfakku ʿan matnihā raʿdu
sentences.l:
No, by her love — an oath by one with passion — * I will honor a dwelling in which Hind has alighted.
Her love is a love that the people know no other than; * so it has no before and it has no after.
As if the dust of the valley were musked with ambergris * when Hind passes one day through its courtyard.
Peace upon a beloved on the hills of the protected pasture, * dear one of a people, everyone around her a slave.
O my two friends, after the evening there is no halting-place; * rest — here are the ban-tree and the lone landmark.
So no postponing — not from other than my heart — for it * is the ally of a passion that cannot be turned back.
May God water Nuzhat al-Zamān with clouds, * pouring ones, from whose back the thunder never lets go.
sentences.i:
Nay, by her love — I swear it as one in the grip of passion — I will honor any dwelling where Hind has taken up her abode.
Her love is a love like no other that people know; it has no before and no after.
It is as though the dust of the valley were scented with musk and ambergris whenever Hind walks one day through its courtyard.
Peace upon a beloved of the hills of the sacred pasture, the dear one of a people, all who surround her her slaves.
O my friends, after this evening there is no resting-place; rest here, where the ban-tree stands and the one lone landmark.
No putting it off, then — and none to blame but my heart — for it is the confederate of a passion that cannot be turned back.
May God send Nuzhat al-Zamān pouring clouds from whose heights the thunder never ceases.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all. The sixth line is obscure and the print may be corrupt there (نسأ لا من غير قلبي); it is translated tentatively. In the last line مسحا is read as مِسَحّ, “pouring (rain)”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ وَسَمِعَتْهُ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ كَشَفَتْ ذَيْلَ السِّتَارَةِ عَنِ الْمَحَفَّةِ وَنَظَرَتْهُ فَلَمَّا وَقَعَ بَصَرُهَا عَلَى وَجْهِهِ عَرَفَتْهُ وَحَقَّقَتْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi wa-samiʿathu nuzhatu al-zamāni kashafat dhayla al-sitārati ʿani al-maḥaffati wa-naẓarathu fa-lammā waqaʿa baṣaruhā ʿalā wajhihi ʿarafathu wa-ḥaqqaqathu
sentences.l: And when he finished from his poetry, and Nuzhat al-Zamān had heard him, she uncovered the hem of the curtain from the litter and looked at him; and when her sight fell upon his face she knew him and made-certain of him.
sentences.i: When he had finished his poem, and Nuzhat al-Zamān had heard it, she drew back the hem of the curtain from the litter and looked at him; and when her eyes fell upon his face she knew him, and made sure.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَتْ قَائِلَةً يَا أَخِي يَا ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ فَنَظَرَ الْآخَرُ إِلَيْهَا فَعَرَفَهَا فَصَاحَ قَائِلًا يَا أُخْتِي يَا نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ فَأَلْقَتْ نَفْسَهَا عَلَيْهِ فَتَلَقَّاهَا فِي حِضْنِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥat qāʾilatan yā akhī yā ḍawʾa al-makāni fa-naẓara al-ākharu ilayhā fa-ʿarafahā fa-ṣāḥa qāʾilan yā ukhtī yā nuzhata al-zamāni fa-alqat nafsahā ʿalayhi fa-talaqqāhā fī ḥiḍnihi
sentences.l: And she cried out, saying: O my brother, O Ḍawʾ al-Makān! And the other looked at her and knew her, and cried out, saying: O my sister, O Nuzhat al-Zamān! And she threw her self upon him, and he met her in his bosom,
sentences.i: She cried out, “O my brother! O Ḍawʾ al-Makān!” The other looked at her and knew her, and cried out, “O my sister! O Nuzhat al-Zamān!” She threw herself upon him, and he received her in his arms,

sentences.t: وَوَقَعَ الِاثْنَانِ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: wa-waqaʿa al-ithnāni maghshiyyan ʿalayhimā
sentences.l: and the two fell, fainted upon them.
sentences.i: and the two of them fell down in a faint.
sentences.n: مغشيا is singular though two people are meant — the agreement is loose, as often in Middle Arabic.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَ هُمَا الْخَادِمُ عَلَى تِلْكَ الْحَالَةِ تَعَجَّبَ فِي أَمْرِهِمَا وَأَلْقَى عَلَيْهِمَا شَيْأً سَتَرَ هُمَا بِهِ وَصَبَرَ عَلَيْهِمَا حَتَّى أَفَاقَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾa humā al-khādimu ʿalā tilka al-ḥālati taʿajjaba fī amrihimā wa-alqā ʿalayhimā shayʾan satara humā bihi wa-ṣabara ʿalayhimā ḥattā afāqā
sentences.l: And when the servant saw them in that state he marveled at their affair, and cast over them something he covered-them with, and was patient with them until they revived.
sentences.i: When the servant saw them in that state he was amazed at what had passed between them; he threw something over them to hide them, and waited patiently beside them until they came to.
sentences.n: The print leaves a space inside رأ هما (for رأى هما, “saw them”) and ستر هما; the spaces are kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَا مِنْ غَشْيَتِهِمَا فَرِحَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ غَايَةَ الْفَرَحِ وَزَالَ عَنْهَا الْهَمُّ وَالتَّرَحُ وَتَوَالَتْ عَلَيْهَا الْمَسَرَّاتُ وَأَنْشَدَتْ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqā min ghashyatihimā fariḥat nuzhatu al-zamāni ghāyata al-faraḥi wa-zāla ʿanhā al-hammu wa-al-taraḥu wa-tawālat ʿalayhā al-masarrātu wa-anshadat hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And when they revived from their swoon, Nuzhat al-Zamān rejoiced the utmost of the joy, and the worry and the sorrow went from her, and the delights followed one after another upon her, and she recited these verses.
sentences.i: When they had come out of their swoon, Nuzhat al-Zamān rejoiced beyond measure; care and sorrow left her, delight followed upon delight, and she recited these verses:

sentences.t:
اَلدَّهْرُ اَقْسَمَ لَا يَزَالُ مُكَدِّرِي * حَنَثَتْ يَمِينُكَ يَا زَمَانُ فَكَفِّرِي
اَلسَّعْدُ وَافَى وَالْحَبِيبُ مُسَاعِدِي * فَانْهَضْ اِلَى دَاعِي السُّرُورِ وَشَمِّرِي
مَا كُنْتُ اَعْتَقِدُ السَّوَالِفَ جَنَّةً * حَتَّى ظَفِرْتُ مِنَ اللَّمَى بِالْكَوْثَرِ
sentences.tr:
al-dahru aqsama lā yazālu mukaddirī * ḥanathat yamīnuka yā zamānu fa-kaffirī
al-saʿdu wafā wa-al-ḥabību musāʿidī * fa-anhaḍ ilā dāʿī al-surūri wa-shammirī
mā kuntu aʿtaqidu al-sawālifa jannatan * ḥattā ẓafirtu mina al-lamā bi-al-kawtharī
sentences.l:
Fate swore that it would never cease to trouble me; * your oath is broken, O Time — so atone!
Good fortune has come and the beloved is my helper; * so rise to the caller of joy and gird yourself!
I did not hold the bygone days a paradise * until I won, from the dusk of the lips, the Kawthar.
sentences.i:
Fate swore it would never cease to cloud my life — your oath is broken, O Time, so make amends!
Fortune has come and my beloved is at my side; rise to the summoner of joy and gird yourself!
I never thought the days gone by a paradise, until I won the Kawthar from the dark lips of my love.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it. السوالف can mean “past times” and also “the side-locks of the hair”; the poem plays on both. The Kawthar is the river of Paradise; اللمى is the dusky shade of beautiful lips.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ذَلِكَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ ضَمَّ أُخْتَهُ إِلَى صَدْرِهِ وَفَاضَتْ لِفَرْطِ سُرُورِهِ مِنْ أَجْفَانِهِ الْعَبَرَاتُ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa dhālika ḍawʾu al-makāni ḍamma ukhtahu ilā ṣadrihi wa-fāḍat li-farṭi surūrihi min ajfānihi al-ʿabarātu wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān heard that, he pressed his sister to his chest, and the tears overflowed from his eyelids from the excess of his joy, and he recited these verses.
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān heard this, he pressed his sister to his breast, and tears overflowed from his eyes in the excess of his joy, and he recited these verses:

sentences.t:
كِلَانَا سَوَاءٌ فِى الْهَوَى غَيْرَ انَّهَا * تَجَلَّدُ اَحْيَانًا وَمَا بِي تَجَلُّدُ
تَخَافُ وَعِيدَ الْكَاشِحِينَ وَاِنَّمَا * جُنُونِي عَلَيْهَا حِينَ انْهَى وَاُوعِدُ
sentences.tr:
kilānā sawāʾun fī al-hawā ghayra annahā * tajalladu aḥyānan wa-mā bī tajalludu
takhāfu waʿīda al-kāshiḥīna wa-innamā * junūnī ʿalayhā ḥīna unhā wa-ūʿidu
sentences.l:
We two are alike in passion, except that she * shows fortitude at times, while in me there is no fortitude.
She fears the threat of the slanderers; but * my madness for her comes when I am forbidden and threatened.
sentences.i:
We are two alike in love, except that she can at times hold firm, while I have no firmness at all.
She fears the threats of the slanderers, whereas my frenzy for her only grows when I am forbidden and threatened.
sentences.n: Verse copied exactly as the edition prints it, marks and all. In the last line the print’s pointing of انهى is kept as it stands; it is read as “I am forbidden”.

sentences.t: وَجَلَسَا عَلَى بَابِ الْمَحَفَّةِ سَاعَةً ثُمَّ قَالَتْ قُمْ بِنَا إِلَى دَاخِلِ الْمَحَفَّةِ وَاحْكِ لِي مَا وَقَعَ لَكَ وَأَنَا أَحْكِي لَكَ عَلَى مَا وَقَعَ لِي فَدَخَلَا
sentences.tr: wa-jalasā ʿalā bābi al-maḥaffati sāʿatan thumma qālat qum bi-nā ilā dākhili al-maḥaffati wa-iḥki lī mā waqaʿa laka wa-anā aḥkī laka ʿalā mā waqaʿa lī fa-dakhalā
sentences.l: And the two sat at the door of the litter for an hour; then she said: Rise with us to the inside of the litter, and tell me what happened to you, and I will tell you what happened to me. And the two entered.
sentences.i: They sat at the door of the litter for a while. Then she said, “Come with me inside the litter. Tell me what has happened to you, and I will tell you what has happened to me.” So the two went in.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُالْمَكَانِ اِحْكِي لِي أَنْتِ أَوَّلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni iḥkī lī anti awwalan
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: Tell me, you, first.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said, “You tell me first.”
sentences.n: The print writes ضوءالمكان as one word here and in several places below; it is kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَحَكَتْ لَهُ جَمِيعَ مَا وَقَعَ لَهَا مُنْذُ فَارَقَتْهُ مِنَ الْخَانِ وَمَا وَقَعَ لَهَا مَعَ الْبَدَوِيِّ وَالتَّاجِرِ وَكَيْفَ اشْتَرَاهَا مِنْهُ وَكَيْفَ أَخَذَهَا التَّاجِرُ إِلَى أَخِيهَا شَرْكَانَ وَبَاعَهَا لَهُ وَأَنَّ شَرْكَانَ أَعْتَقَهَا مِنْ حِينِ اشْتَرَاهَا وَكَتَبَ كِتَابَهُ عَلَيْهَا وَدَخَلَ بِهَا وَأَنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَبُوهَا سَمِعَ بِخَبَرِهَا فَأَرْسَلَ إِىٰ شَرْكَانَ يَطْلُبُهَا مِنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakat lahu jamīʿa mā waqaʿa lahā mundhu fāraqathu mina al-khāni wa-mā waqaʿa lahā maʿa al-badawiyyi wa-al-tājiri wa-kayfa ishtarāhā minhu wa-kayfa akhadhahā al-tājiru ilā akhīhā sharkāna wa-bāʿahā lahu wa-anna sharkāna aʿtaqahā min ḥīni ishtarāhā wa-kataba kitābahu ʿalayhā wa-dakhala bihā wa-anna al-malika abūhā samiʿa bi-khabarihā fa-arsala ilā sharkāna yaṭlubuhā minhu
sentences.l: And she told him all that had happened to her since she parted from him, from the inn, and what happened to her with the Bedouin and the merchant, and how he bought her from him, and how the merchant took her to her brother Sharkān and sold her to him, and that Sharkān freed her from the time he bought her, and wrote his writing upon her, and went in to her, and that the king her father heard of her news and sent to Sharkān, asking her from him.
sentences.i: She told him everything that had happened to her since she parted from him at the inn: what befell her with the Bedouin and the merchant, how the merchant bought her from the Bedouin, and how he took her to her brother Sharkān and sold her to him; that Sharkān freed her from the moment he bought her, drew up his marriage contract with her and went in to her; and that the king, their father, had heard word of her and sent to Sharkān to ask for her back.
sentences.n: أى in the print stands for إلى; it is pointed with the dagger alif as a defective spelling. كتب كتابه عليها is “drew up his contract with her” — the marriage contract.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي مَنَّ عَلَيَّ بِكَ وَمِثْلَ مَا خَرَجْنَا مِنْ عِنْدِ وَالِدِنَا سَوَاءً نَرْجِعُ إِلَيْهِ سَوَاءً
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu al-ḥamdu li-allāhi alladhī manna ʿalayya bi-ka wa-mithla mā kharajnā min ʿindi wālidinā sawāʾan narjiʿu ilayhi sawāʾan
sentences.l: Then she said to him: Praise be to God who has bestowed upon me with you; and like what we went out from beside our father, equal, we return to him, equal.
sentences.i: Then she said to him, “Praise be to God, who has shown me this grace in you! Just as we left our father’s house together, so together we shall return to him.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّ أَخِي شَرْكَانَ زَوَّجَنِي بِهَذَا الْحَاجِبِ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ يُوصِلَنِي إِلَى وَالِدِي وَهَذَا مَا وَقَعَ لِي مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat lahu inna akhī sharkāna zawwajanī bi-hādhā al-ḥājibi li-ajli an yūṣilanī ilā wālidī wa-hādhā mā waqaʿa lī mina al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri
sentences.l: Then she said to him: My brother Sharkān married me to this chamberlain, for the sake that he bring me to my father; and this is what happened to me from the first to the last.
sentences.i: Then she said to him, “My brother Sharkān married me to this chamberlain so that he might bring me to my father. That is all that has happened to me, from first to last.”

sentences.t: فَاحْكِ لِي أَنْتَ مَا وَقَعَ لَكَ بَعْدَ ذَهَابِي مِنْ عِنْدِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-iḥki lī anta mā waqaʿa laka baʿda dhahābī min ʿindika
sentences.l: So tell me, you, what happened to you after my going from beside you.
sentences.i: Now you tell me what happened to you after I left you.”

sentences.t: فَحَكَى لَهَا جَمِيعَ مَا وَقَعَ لَهُ مِنَ الْأَوَّلِ إِلَى الْآخِرِ وَكَيْفَ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ بِالْوَقَّادِ وَكَيْفَ سَافَرَ مَعَهُ وَأَنْفَقَ عَلَيْهِ مَالَهُ وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَخْدُمُهُ فِى اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ فَشَكَرَتْهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakā lahā jamīʿa mā waqaʿa lahu mina al-awwali ilā al-ākhiri wa-kayfa manna allāhu ʿalayhi bi-al-waqqādi wa-kayfa sāfara maʿahu wa-anfaqa ʿalayhi mālahu wa-annahu kāna yakhdumuhu fī al-layli wa-al-nahāri fa-shakarathu ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And he told her all that had happened to him from the first to the last, and how God bestowed upon him the stoker, and how he travelled with him, and spent his money on him, and that he used to serve him in the night and the day; and she thanked him for that.
sentences.i: He told her everything that had happened to him from first to last: how God had shown him grace through the stoker, how he had travelled with him and spent his own money on him, and how he had served him night and day. She thanked the stoker for that.
sentences.n: The stoker (الوقاد) is the bath-house fire-tender who took Ḍawʾ al-Makān in and travelled with him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهَا يَا أُخْتِي إِنَّ هَذَا الْوَقَّادَ فَعَلَ مَعِي مِنَ الْإِحْسَانِ فِعْلًا لَا يَفْعَلُهُ أَحَدٌ فِي أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَحْبَابِهِ وَلَا الْوَالِدُ مَعَ وَالِدِهِ حَتَّى كَانَ يَجُوعُ وَيُطْعِمُنِي وَيَمْشِي وَيُرْكِبُنِي وَكَانَتْ حَيَاتِي عَلَى يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahā yā ukhtī inna hādhā al-waqqāda faʿala maʿī mina al-iḥsāni fiʿlan lā yafʿaluhu aḥadun fī aḥadin min aḥbābihi wa-lā al-wālidu maʿa wālidihi ḥattā kāna yajūʿu wa-yuṭʿimunī wa-yamshī wa-yurkibunī wa-kānat ḥayātī ʿalā yadayhi
sentences.l: Then he said to her: O my sister, this stoker did with me, of kindness, a deed that no one does to anyone of his loved-ones, nor the father with his father, until he would go hungry and feed me, and walk and make-me-ride; and my life was upon his two hands.
sentences.i: Then he said to her, “My sister, this stoker showed me such kindness as no one shows to any of his dearest friends — not even a father to his own son. He would go hungry so that I could eat, and walk so that I could ride; my very life was in his hands.”
sentences.n: والده is printed where one expects ولده, “his son”; it is vocalised as printed and translated by the sense.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ نُزْهَةُالزَّمَانِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى نُكَافِئُهُ بِمَا نَقْدِرُ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu nuzhatu al-zamāni in shāʾa allāhu taʿālā nukāfiʾuhu bi-mā naqdiru ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And Nuzhat al-Zamān said to him: If God the Exalted wills, we will repay him with what we are able to.
sentences.i: Nuzhat al-Zamān said to him, “If God Most High wills, we shall repay him with whatever is in our power.”
sentences.n: The print writes نزهةالزمان as one word here and below.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ صَاحَتْ عَلَى الْخَادِمِ فَحَضَرَ وَقَبَّلَ يَدَ ضَوْءِالْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna nuzhata al-zamāni ṣāḥat ʿalā al-khādimi fa-ḥaḍara wa-qabbala yada ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān called out to the servant, and he came, and kissed the hand of Ḍawʾ al-Makān,
sentences.i: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān called to the servant; he came and kissed Ḍawʾ al-Makān’s hand,

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ لَهُ نُزْهَةُالزَّمَانِ خُذْ بِشَارَتَكَ يَا وَجْهَ الْخَيْرِ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ جَمَعَ شَمْلِي بِأَخِي عَلَى يَدَيْكَ فَالْكِيسُ الَّذِي مَعَكَ وَمَا فِيهِ لَكَ فَاذْهَبْ وَائْتِنِي بِسَيِّدِكَ عَاجِلًا
sentences.tr: wa-qālat lahu nuzhatu al-zamāni khudh bishārataka yā wajha al-khayri li-annahu kāna jamaʿa shamlī bi-akhī ʿalā yadayka fa-al-kīsu alladhī maʿaka wa-mā fīhi laka fa-idhhab wa-ʾtinī bi-sayyidika ʿājilan
sentences.l: and Nuzhat al-Zamān said to him: Take your good-tidings-gift, O face of goodness, because he had gathered my union with my brother upon your two hands; so the purse that is with you and what is in it is yours. So go and bring me your master quickly.
sentences.i: and Nuzhat al-Zamān said to him, “Take your reward for good news, O bringer of good fortune, for it was through your hands that I was joined again with my brother. The purse you carry, and all that is in it, is yours. Now go and bring me your master, quickly.”
sentences.n: لأنه is printed as a third-person pronoun (“because he …”); the sense is that God has reunited her through the servant’s hands, and it is translated so.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْخَادِمُ وَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى الْحَاجِبِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ وَدَعَاهُ إِلَى سَيِّدَتِهِ فَأَتَى بِهِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى زَوْجَتِهِ نُزْهَةِالزَّمَانِ فَوَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا أَخَاهَا فَسَأَلَ عَنْهُ فَحَكَتْ لَهُ مَاوَقَعَ لَهُمَا مِنْ أَوَّلِهِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-khādimu wa-tawajjaha ilā al-ḥājibi wa-dakhala ʿalayhi wa-daʿāhu ilā sayyidatihi fa-atā bihi wa-dakhala ʿalā zawjatihi nuzhati al-zamāni fa-wajada ʿindahā akhāhā fa-saʾala ʿanhu fa-ḥakat lahu mā waqaʿa lahumā min awwalihi ilā ākhirihi
sentences.l: And the servant rejoiced and made his way to the chamberlain, and entered upon him, and called him to his mistress; and he came with him, and entered upon his wife Nuzhat al-Zamān, and found her brother with her, and asked about him; and she told him what had happened to the two of them, from its beginning to its end.
sentences.i: The servant was overjoyed. He went to the chamberlain, came in to him, and called him to his mistress; and the chamberlain came with him and went in to his wife, Nuzhat al-Zamān. He found her brother with her and asked who he was, and she told him all that had happened to the two of them, from beginning to end.
sentences.n: ماوقع is printed as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتِ اعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْحَاجِبُ أَنَّكَ مَا أَخَذْتَ جَارِيَةً وَإِنَّمَا أَخَذْتَ بِنْتَ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ فَأَنَا نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ وَهَذَا أَخِي ضَوْءُالْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma qālati iʿlam ayyuhā al-ḥājibu annaka mā akhadhta jāriyatan wa-innamā akhadhta binta al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni fa-anā nuzhatu al-zamāni wa-hādhā akhī ḍawʾu al-makāni
sentences.l: Then she said: Know, O chamberlain, that you did not take a slave-girl, but you took the daughter of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān; for I am Nuzhat al-Zamān, and this is my brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: Then she said, “Know, chamberlain, that you have not taken a slave-girl; you have taken the daughter of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. I am Nuzhat al-Zamān, and this is my brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān.”

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْحَاجِبُ الْقِصَّةَ مِنْهَا تَحَقَّقَ مَاقَالَتْهُ وَبَانَ لَهُ الْحَقُّ الصَّرِيحُ وَتَيَقَّنَ أَنَّهُ صَارَ صِهْرَ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ فَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ مَصِيرِي أَنْ آخُذَ نِيَابَةً عَلَى قُطْرٍ مِنَ الْأَقْطَارِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-ḥājibu al-qiṣṣata minhā taḥaqqaqa mā qālathu wa-bāna lahu al-ḥaqqu al-ṣarīḥu wa-tayaqqana annahu ṣāra ṣihra al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni fa-qāla fī nafsihi maṣīrī an ākhudha niyābatan ʿalā quṭrin mina al-aqṭāri
sentences.l: And when the chamberlain heard the story from her, he verified what she had said, and the pure truth became clear to him, and he was certain that he had become son-in-law of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān; and he said in himself: My destination is that I take a deputyship over a region of the regions.
sentences.i: When the chamberlain heard the story from her, he accepted what she said; the plain truth was clear to him, and he was certain that he had become the son-in-law of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. He said to himself, “I am bound to end up with a governorship over some province or other.”
sentences.n: ماقالته is printed as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَهَنَّأَهُ بِسَلَامَتِهِ وَجَمْعِ شَمْلِهِ بِأُخْتِهِ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ خَدَمَهُ فِى الْحَالِ أَنْ يُهَيِّئُوا لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ خَيْمَةً وَمَرْكُوبًا مِنْ أَحْسَنِ الْخَيْلِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala ʿalā ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-hannaʾahu bi-salāmatihi wa-jamʿi shamlihi bi-ukhtihi thumma amara khadamahu fī al-ḥāli an yuhayyiʾū li-ḍawʾi al-makāni khaymatan wa-markūban min aḥsani al-khayli
sentences.l: Then he turned toward Ḍawʾ al-Makān and congratulated him on his safety and the gathering of his union with his sister; then he ordered his servants at once to prepare for Ḍawʾ al-Makān a tent and a mount from the best of horses.
sentences.i: Then he turned to Ḍawʾ al-Makān and congratulated him on his safety and on being reunited with his sister. He ordered his servants at once to prepare a tent for Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and a mount from among the finest horses.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أُخْتُهُ إِنَّا قَدْ قَرُبْنَا مِنْ بِلَادِنَا فَأَنَا أَخْتَلِي بِأَخِي وَنَسْتَرِيحُ مَعَ بَعْضِنَا وَنَشْبَعُ مِنْ بَعْضِنَا قَبْلَ أَنْ نَصِلَ إِلَى بِلَادِنَا فَإِنَّ لَنَا زَمَنًا طَوِيلًا وَنَحْنُ مُفْتَرِقَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ukhtuhu innā qad qarubnā min bilādinā fa-anā akhtalī bi-akhī wa-nastarīḥu maʿa baʿḍinā wa-nashbaʿu min baʿḍinā qabla an naṣila ilā bilādinā fa-inna lanā zamanan ṭawīlan wa-naḥnu muftariqāni
sentences.l: And his sister said to him: We have drawn near to our country, so I will be alone with my brother, and we rest with one another, and we are sated of one another, before we reach our country; for we have had a long time while we are two parted ones.
sentences.i: His sister said to him, “We have come near our own country, so I would like to be alone with my brother. We shall rest together and take our fill of one another before we reach our land, for we have been parted a long time.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْحَاجِبُ الْأَمْرُكَمَا تُرِيدَانِ ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِمَا الشُّمُوعَ وَأَنْوَاعَ الْحَلَاوَةِ وَخَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ḥājibu al-amru kamā turīdāni thumma arsala ilayhimā al-shumūʿa wa-anwāʿa al-ḥalāwati wa-kharaja min ʿindihimā
sentences.l: And the chamberlain said: The matter is as you two wish. Then he sent to them the candles and kinds of sweetmeats, and went out from beside them.
sentences.i: “It shall be as you both wish,” said the chamberlain. Then he sent them candles and all kinds of sweetmeats, and left them.
sentences.n: الأمركما is printed as one word.

sentences.t: وَأَرْسَلَ إِلَى ضَوْءِالْمَكَانِ ثَلٰثَ بَدَلَاتٍ مِنْ أَفْخَرِ الثِّيَابِ وَتَمَشَّي إِلَى أَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى الْمَصَفَّةِ وَعَرَفَ مِقْدَارَ نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-arsala ilā ḍawʾi al-makāni thalātha badalātin min afkhari al-thiyābi wa-tamashshā ilā an jāʾa ilā al-maṣaffati wa-ʿarafa miqdāra nafsihi
sentences.l: And he sent to Ḍawʾ al-Makān three suits of the most splendid of garments, and walked until he came to the litter, and knew the measure of himself.
sentences.i: He sent Ḍawʾ al-Makān three suits of the most splendid clothes, and walked until he reached the litter, mindful of his place.
sentences.n: ثلث is the edition’s defective spelling of ثلاث, pointed with the dagger alif. المصفة is evidently a misprint for المحفة, “the litter”; it is vocalised as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ أَرْسِلْ إِلَى الْخَادِمِ وَأْمُرْهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْوَقَّادِ وَيُهَيِّءَ لَهُ حِصَانًا يَرْكَبُهُ وَيُرَتِّبَ لَهُ سُفْرَةَ طَعَامٍ فِى الْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ وَيَأْمُرَهُ أَنَّهُ لَايُفَارِقُنَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu nuzhatu al-zamāni arsil ilā al-khādimi wa-ʾmurhu an yaʾtiya bi-al-waqqādi wa-yuhayyiʾa lahu ḥiṣānan yarkabuhu wa-yurattiba lahu sufrata ṭaʿāmin fī al-ghadāti wa-al-ʿashiyyi wa-yaʾmurahu annahu lā yufāriqunā
sentences.l: And Nuzhat al-Zamān said to him: Send to the servant and command him to come with the stoker, and to make ready for him a horse he may ride, and to arrange for him a table of food in the morning and the evening, and to command him that he not leave us.
sentences.i: Nuzhat al-Zamān said to him, “Send to the servant and tell him to bring the stoker, to find him a horse to ride and to set him a table of food morning and evening, and tell him he is never to leave us.”
sentences.n: لايفارقنا is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَرْسَلَ الْحَاجِبُ إِلَى الْخَادِمِ وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَفْعَلَ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika arsala al-ḥājibu ilā al-khādimi wa-amarahu an yafʿala dhālika fa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And at that, the chamberlain sent to the servant and commanded him to do that; and he said: With hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: Then the chamberlain sent to the servant and told him to do so, and the servant answered, “With hearing and obedience.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَادِمَ أَخَذَ غِلْمَانَهُ وَذَهَبَ يُفَتِّشُ عَلَى الْوَقَّادِ إِلَى أَنْ وَجَدَهُ فِي آخِرِ الرَّكْبِ وَهُوَ يَشُدُّ حِمَارَهُ وَيُرِيدُأَنْ يَهْرُبَ وَدُمُوعُهُ تَجْرِي عَلَى خَدِّهِ مِنَ الْخَوْفِ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَمِنْ حُزْنِهِ عَلَى فِرَاقِ ضَوْءِالْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khādima akhadha ghilmānahu wa-dhahaba yufattishu ʿalā al-waqqādi ilā an wajadahu fī ākhiri al-rakbi wa-huwa yashuddu ḥimārahu wa-yurīdu an yahruba wa-dumūʿuhu tajrī ʿalā khaddihi mina al-khawfi ʿalā nafsihi wa-min ḥuznihi ʿalā firāqi ḍawʾi al-makāni
sentences.l: Then the servant took his boys and went searching for the stoker, until he found him at the rear of the caravan, tightening his donkey, wanting to flee, his tears running down his cheek from fear for himself and from his grief at the parting from Ḍawʾ al-Makān,
sentences.i: Then the servant took his men and went looking for the stoker, until he found him at the tail of the caravan, cinching his donkey and about to run away, his tears running down his cheeks from fear for himself and grief at being parted from Ḍawʾ al-Makān,
sentences.n: ويريدان is printed as one word: يريد أن, “wants to”.

sentences.t: وَصَارَ يَقُولُ قَلْ نَصَحْتُهُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَلَمْ يَسْمَعْ مِنِّي يَاتَرَى كَيْفَ حَالُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣāra yaqūlu qal naṣaḥtuhu fī sabīli allāhi fa-lam yasmaʿ minnī yā tarā kayfa ḥāluhu
sentences.l: and he began to say: I advised him, for the sake of God, and he did not listen to me. I wonder how his state is.
sentences.i: and he kept saying, “I advised him, for God’s sake, and he would not listen to me. I wonder how he is.”
sentences.n: قل is probably a misprint for قد (“indeed I advised him”); it is vocalised as printed. ياترى is printed as one word, a common colloquial “I wonder”.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَتِمَّ كَلَامُهُ إِلَّا وَالْخَادِمُ وَاقِفٌ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ وَدَارَتْ حَوْلَهُ الْغِلْمَانُ فَالْتَفَتَ الْوَقَّادُ فَرَأَى الْخَادِمَ وَاقِفًا فَوْقَ رَأْسِهِ وَرَأَى الْغِلْمَانَ حَوْلَهُ فَاصْفَرَّ لَوْنُهُ وَخَافَ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yatimma kalāmuhu illā wa-al-khādimu wāqifun ʿalā raʾsihi wa-dārat ḥawlahu al-ghilmānu fa-iltafata al-waqqādu fa-raʾā al-khādima wāqifan fawqa raʾsihi wa-raʾā al-ghilmāna ḥawlahu fa-iṣfarra lawnuhu wa-khāfa
sentences.l: And his speech was not complete but the servant was standing over his head, and the boys had circled around him; and the stoker turned and saw the servant standing above his head, and saw the boys around him, and his colour turned yellow, and he was afraid,
sentences.i: He had hardly finished speaking when the servant was standing over him and the men had closed in around him. The stoker turned and saw the servant standing above his head and the men all about him; his face went yellow with fear,

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ الْمُبْ—احِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the speech the permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech unspoken.
sentences.n: The stock close of a night. The print repeats the last word, the second copy damaged (المب—اح); it is read as a stray repeat of al-mubāḥ.
